page: Microsoft Azure E32_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance running on Microsoft Hyper-V. The server is powered by a dedicated 2.8 GHz Intel Xeon Platinum 8370C processor built on the x86_64 architecture. It features 16 physical cores configured with two hardware threads per core, presenting 32 vCPUs to the guest operating system. The processor cache hierarchy includes 48 KB of L1 data cache per core, 1 MB of L2 cache per core, and a shared 48 MB L3 cache. It incorporates vector and cryptographic instruction set extensions including AVX-512, AVX-512 VNNI, VAES, and SHA-NI.

The system provides 256 GB of system RAM, maintaining an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio. In synthetic benchmarks, the memory subsystem achieved a PassMark memory score of 2,786.13, placing it in the top 25 percent tier, alongside an uncached read bandwidth of 149.09 GB/s and write bandwidth of 69.17 GB/s. The server lacks bundled local storage and contains no discrete GPU accelerators, requiring attached remote network volumes for persistent block storage. It also includes zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Across compute and database tests, the E32_v5 shows solid mid-tier performance, producing a Geekbench 6 multi-core score of 14,055.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 36,942.62. In in-memory data processing, it handled 31.47 million Redis SET operations per second and scored 15,218.08 in PassMark database operations. Image processing on Geekbench placed in the top 25 percent with 13,595.0 points. While small 135M language model generation reached 305.89 tokens per second, large model execution is limited due to the absence of hardware accelerators.

Given its high memory density and absence of local storage, the E32_v5 is cost-effective for large memory footprints where compute density is secondary. It is well structured for in-memory caching layers, relational databases, enterprise resource planning, and intermediate data processing jobs.
description: Microsoft Azure E32_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine powered by an Intel Xeon Platinum 8370C processor running at 2.8 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The instance provides 32 dedicated vCPUs derived from 16 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading, alongside 48 MB of L3 cache and AVX-512 vector support. Memory capacity is substantial at 256 GB, providing an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio that yields top-tier memory benchmark scores. The instance includes no onboard local storage, zero GPUs, and no complimentary public IPv4 addresses, necessitating remote managed disks for persistent operations. Compute benchmarks place the instance squarely in the median range for general CPU processing, while in-memory operations remain strong with 31.47 million Redis SET operations per second. This instance is specifically configured for memory-bound enterprise workloads, including large in-memory caches, relational database systems, and data transformation pipelines that require significant RAM capacity.
